best_for: People who live in WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram and a few web apps at once and want them in one window, with no subscription and no account required.

points.title: Many chat apps, one window
points.text: Each service runs in its own tab, and you can add the same one twice for two logins, such as a work and a personal Slack. Custom services cover web apps that are not in the store.

points.title: No account unless you want sync
points.text: You can use it without signing up. An account only adds cloud sync, so your services and workspaces follow you to another computer.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Ferdium is a community hard fork of Franz under the Apache 2.0 license, and the site shows no paid plan. It works with existing Franz accounts and can migrate Ferdi profiles.

points.title: Keeps work and home apart
points.text: Workspaces show only the services that belong together, and idle services can hibernate to save memory. A built-in to-do panel sits next to your chats.

points.title: Get it from the real site
points.text: The project warns that ferdium.org is its only official domain and that look-alike sites have spread malware. Official builds are published on the project's GitHub releases page.

points.title: Builds per platform
points.text: Windows installers come in x86, x64 and Arm64, and this site keeps 31 Windows versions. The Mac DMGs, for Intel and Apple silicon, need macOS 12 or later. The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub as published by the Ferdium Team. Mac and Linux list only the current release here.
